Previous posts have looked at the range of zoning in the city of Franklin and how much property the city owns. This post will look at some of these properties over time to understand changing assessments and the tax cap. The data for this post come from NH tax kiosk, the online portal used to pay taxes. I gathered this data in late 2025, so it may have changed since then, but I believe it is complete enough for this analysis. This post will not name individual property owners, instead it will examine, in aggregate, the changes in assessment.

Below is a map that I a going to be using to look at downtown vs. lake. I’ve used two zoning overlays to filter the relevant parcels, Lake protection district, and Downtown revitalization overlay district. This post seeks to answer the question: are both of these sections of the city contributing equally to the tax base?

First, let’s look at the number of properties in each, and their type. The below map looks at the land use parameter on the tax card - this idetifies each parcel in categories like 1 family residential (1F residential), 2 family residential (2F residential), commercial/industrial (COM/IND). Note that this is not zoning, this is the use of the property. It’s also not perfect, some parcels are missing classifications, and others may be misclassified.

Going into this, my intuition is that the lake will be dominated by single family residential, while the downtown will be multifamily and commerical.
